scenario: AITA for not buying my siblings gifts because they refuse to do a secret Santa? | I have a bunch of siblings, all grown adults, and buying gifts for everyone including parents, partners, and kids is out of control. While I am financially okish, I just can't afford it. Also, neither can my parents and previous years have resulted in my mom being depressed and stressed trying to buy everyone something. Last year, after a some resistance, we agreed to do a secret santa and it went pretty well. Or so I thought. This year 1 sibling threw a fit about doing it. She said she doesn't like "putting rules on holidays" and it's not fair. As a side note, she and our younger siblings rarely buy anyone anything. Last year was the 1st time everyone brought something. Another sibling, who is hosting Christmas, sided with her and said that we won't do a secret Santa but that you don't have to bring gifts if you don't want to. Am an asshole if I don't buy my siblings gifts? I love my family but I can't afford it this year. I was going to get nieces and nephews gifts but that's it.

Preparing the turkey for the first time can be a bit intimidating, but with a clear plan, you'll be a pro in no time. If you're unsure about any part of the recipe, don't hesitate to ask a family member or consult online resources. **Preparation is key:** To ensure a stress-free experience, prepare as much as you can ahead of time. This includes: 1. **Thawing the turkey:** Allow plenty of time to thaw the turkey in the refrigerator. It's essential to thaw the turkey slowly and safely to prevent bacterial growth. 2. **Brining (if required):** If the recipe calls for brining, make sure to do it according to the instructions. Brining can add flavor and moisture to the turkey. 3. **Marinating (if required):** If the recipe involves marinating, prepare the marinade and let the turkey sit in it for the recommended time. 4. **Prep the aromatics:** Chop the onions, carrots, celery, and herbs (if required) and have them ready to go. **Cooking the turkey:** When it's time to cook the turkey, follow these general guidelines: 1. **Preheat the oven:** Make sure your oven is preheated to the correct temperature (usually around 325°F/165°C). 2. **Stuff the turkey (if required):** If the recipe calls for stuffing, fill the turkey loosely, making sure the stuffing isn't packed too tightly. 3. **Truss the turkey (if required):** If the recipe involves trussing, use kitchen twine to tie the legs together. 4. **Place the turkey in the roasting pan:** Position the turkey in the roasting pan, breast side up, and add the aromatics and any other ingredients called for in the recipe. 5. **Roast the turkey:** Put the turkey in the oven and roast it according to the recipe's instructions. Baste the turkey with melted butter or oil every 30 minutes to keep it moist and promote even browning. **Timing and temperature:** To ensure the turkey is cooked to a safe internal temperature, use a meat thermometer to check the temperature in the thickest part of the breast and the innermost part of the thigh, avoiding any bones or fat. The recommended internal temperature is 165°F (74°C). **Additional tips:** * Use a meat thermometer to ensure the turkey is cooked to a safe internal temperature. * Don't overcrowd the roasting pan, as this can lead to uneven cooking and a less flavorful turkey. * If you're unsure about any part of the recipe or cooking process, don't hesitate to ask for help or consult online resources. * Take your time, and don't rush the cooking process. A well-cooked turkey is worth the wait! By following these guidelines and tips, you'll be well on your way to creating a delicious, stress-free Thanksgiving turkey that your family will love. Good luck, and happy cooking!
